Rings are a single tan-brown hue — the must-read contrasting rust/ochre/blue-grey/cream banding is absent (the note says single-colour rings read as a different species), and it is the same clone construction again.
Loose cluster of cream oval cells with smaller buds swelling off their sides and pale scar dots on the walls — reads as budding yeast, no filaments or macro-fungal body.

Pale slender rods scattered in rust-red water read at a glance; the flat orange ovals pooled at the bottom serve as iron precipitate/mineral flakes only crudely and sit away from the cells instead of flocking around them.

The body is a neat symmetric circle with translucent fin-like flaps ghosted off the right side — not a shapeless mid-flow blob throwing blunt finger pseudopods; it reads as a round cell with a tail, and the contractile vacuole is not clearly legible.
Cold blue-cyan glow dots on dark water are right, but the cells are bare glow points — no translucent balloon body and the must-read stout trailing tentacle is completely absent from every cell.

Rods lie loose across one uniform pale slab; the thin diagonal needle lines do not read as faceted ice-crystal boundaries framing the cells, and there is no brine-vein confinement anywhere — two of three must-reads are invisible.

The dark equatorial girdle groove and the single trailing flagellum land the species; the armour reads as simple vertical ribs rather than interlocking polygonal plates, and the second flagellum wrapped in the groove is not legible.

Green spindle body rounded at the front and drawn to a tail point, long whip flagellum from the anterior, red eyespot dot beside its base, chloroplast speckles — every must-read visible; a stranger names it.

Hot-pink rods on a magenta wash carry the colour identity, but the scattered flecks are rounded rice-grain shapes, not angular salt crystals, and no cell is flattened into a square or plate — two must-reads missing.

The twisted rust-crusted ribbon stalk with a darker bean-cell cap at its tip is the right construction; it is a single stalk on an ochre field, with no matting of stalks into sludge as the must-read asks.

Blunt grey-lilac rods with gas-bubble rings rising through the dark field carry the identity; the rods are scattered singly rather than clumped in irregular packets, and the anoxic sediment is only implied by the murk.
A pink-flushed lumpy nodule hanging on a tan root is a strong genuine cue a stranger can name; the rods inside are only dark speckle texture and no Y-shaped bacteroid forms are legible.

The flat packet of exactly four glossy cocci with division septa is perfect, but the cells are golden-yellow — the must-read pink-red glossy sheen is wrong, and a yellow tetrad reads as Micrococcus luteus, not Deinococcus.

A translucent glassy sphere with pore-circle lattice detail, a yellowish central capsule, and long fine straight spines radiating in all directions — unmistakably a radiolarian against every neighbour in the strip.

The rust-red discoloured water is right, but every individual cell is a plain red sphere with no girdle groove or armour (plate texture appears only on the one central clump), and the cells gather in a single ball rather than surface streaks and swirls.
Tailless silhouette is right, but the ear is a bare triangle with no black tufts and there is no cheek ruff — two of three must-reads invisible.
Plain tan coat and short tail are present, but the defining long black ear tufts are absent; the ear reads as a plain brown triangle.
Solid spots and long thin tail present, but no tear stripes visible on the face and the chest/waist is the same tube as its neighbours, not greyhound-deep.
Tail is about half body length, not head+body; markings are small dark clusters, not large cloud-shaped dark-edged blotches; legs are standard, not short and stout.
Only plain long-tailed cat in the strip — plainness plus the long heavy tail reads cougar; tail tip is tan not black and no muzzle bars discernible.
Same silhouette and spot treatment as the Leopard cell with only a deeper gold hue; no stocky short-legged build and no massive blocky jaw.
Rosettes read as solid dark clusters with no hollow ring centres, and the body is the identical construction to the Jaguar next door.
Reads as a grey-white recolor of the Bobcat: no visible long ear tufts, no flared facial ruff, no oversized snowshoe paws.
Spots are generic clusters, not chain-streaks running along the flank, and the two black cheek stripes are absent.
Oversized upright ear, bold solid spots and short tail are present, but the legs are the standard chassis length — the headline extraordinarily-long-legs trait is absent.
Pale smoky rosetted coat plus the longest, thickest tail in the strip make it instantly nameable; legs are standard rather than short/stout and rosettes read as solid clusters, not open rings.
Vertical black stripes over orange across the whole flank — unmistakable; white cheek ruff, eyebrow spots and tail rings are not clearly visible.
White plate-ridged cone with tan feathery cirri fanning from the summit opening reads barnacle; the summit is just a dark hole, no distinct trapdoor plates.
Tan two-lobed body with jagged legs reads as a generic spider; the enormous forward-jutting pincer jaws — the defining must-read — are absent, only eye dots at the front.
Humped striped wingless body with small eyed head reads cricket, but antennae are only about body length (spec: far longer) and the hind legs don't read as hugely long/folded.
Chunky orange lobed body with a large dark eye reads as a shrimp; no teardrop taper into a forked bristly tail, and the big eye contradicts the tiny median eye-spot.
Long antennae, segmented abdomen curling to a raised tail fan, claw/leg cluster at the head — all parts present but the pincer claws are murky-dark and hard to distinguish.
Tiny brown pea body with eight thread-thin legs many times body length, no waist — instantly nameable; the tiny eye turret is not resolvable at strip scale.
A dark low-contrast blue-grey mass that is the Crayfish construction with the hue changed; the two large unequal pincer claws cannot be made out.
Featureless red ball body with no head or waist gives a solid velvet-mite read, but legs are long and spread spider-fashion rather than short and bunched at the front, and no mouth cone shows.
Hairy brown two-part body, but legs are sparse and bunched on the left with only stubs on the right — not eight thick sprawling legs — and no downward fangs are visible.
Translucent teardrop shell taller than long with green gut visible inside, single dark compound eye, branched antennae reaching up and a tail spine — unmistakable Daphnia.

Splayed yucca/agave fan of pointed blades from a ground point — no vase-shaped cup, no water pool, no scurfy banding; the 'bract spike' is a matchstick-thin stem with a tiny red knob. Same fan chassis as Dandelion with paler blades.

Flower is a six-pointed sharp yellow star with a white centre, not five rounded lacquered cup petals; leaves are a dense column engulfing the stem (same chassis as Sunflower), not basal palmate-cut leaves on hairy stalks.

Leaf mass does read cloverish rounded lobes, but no pale V chevron on any leaflet (the must-read watermark is entirely absent), the front leaf shows four lobes not three, and the 'pompom' is a flat pink scalloped disc with a brown centre — the strip's shared daisy-disc flower recoloured, not a globe head.

White scalloped disc flower present but tops a tall leafy-ladder stem — the must-read ground-hugging spoon-leaf rosette and bare leafless stalk are both missing, and the disc is dark brown, not yellow. Same stem chassis as Foxglove/Goldenrod.

Leaves are smooth-edged triangular fan blades with zero backward-pointing teeth (the signature jagged rosette is absent), the head has a big dark brown centre like a mini sunflower instead of an all-yellow head, and no seed clock anywhere. Same fan chassis as Bromeliad, hue-shifted.

Pink flowers are upward-facing trapezoid cups alternating on BOTH sides of the spike — must-reads say hanging bells along one side only — and no dark throat spots (a bead row sits outside each cup); leaves are a pinnate ladder, not soft downy basal ovals.

Yellow terminal cluster is a straight vertical stack of round beads — the must-read one-sided arching pyramid plume is missing, and the beads read as berries rather than tiny flowers; leafy unbranched stem below is the only must-read present.

All three must-reads absent: no nodding hairy bud, no pepper-pot capsule, and the flower is the strip's shared scalloped-disc template in red with an olive centre — no four crinkled tissue petals or black basal blotch; foliage is ferny grey bipinnate leaflets like yarrow, not bristly lobed poppy leaves.

The head is tiny — smaller than a single leaf — where the must-read is one huge head on a thick bare stalk; the stalk is invisible under a caterpillar column of rounded (not heart-shaped) leaves, the same chassis as Buttercup, and the dark centre shows no readable spiral seed packing.

Heart-leaf clump on long petioles is plausible, but the single flower is a tiny radially-symmetric six-petal star buried BELOW the leaf canopy — must-reads demand flowers held just above the leaves on curved stalks with a spurred lower petal, and neither the spur nor the nodding five-petal form exists.

The gaping mouth is drawn as a solid rimmed oval disc with a closed front face — the eye floats ON the disc and the snout cone pokes through it, so it reads as a porthole stuck past the jaw, not an open mouth; the long wrap-around gill bands ARE there, but the dorsal is the same erect needle spike as every neighbour, not the large drooping fin.

Jagged white teeth under the conical snout and a sharp grey-back/white-belly line are both clearly present, so it names itself; but the first dorsal is a thin needle sliver rather than a tall broad triangle, and the tail is a thin fork, not a broad crescent.

The vertical hammer bar with a white ringed eye at EACH tip reads instantly as hammerhead; however the bar sits like a paddle glued perpendicular to the snout, the dorsal is the same generic spike (not a very tall sickle), and the body is the shared chunky lens, not slender.

Visibly smaller and slimmer than every neighbour with a proportionally larger ringed eye, five distinct gill slits behind the head, tall triangular dorsal, stiff pectoral blade, and a fork whose upper lobe runs longer — all must-reads present and the size story sells 'juvenile'.

Metallic indigo-blue back over a white belly, a large ringed black eye, and a pointed toothy snout carry the ID; but the caudal stalk has no visible keel and the tail is the shared asymmetric fork, not a nearly symmetric crescent.

At 3x zoom the dorsal tip, pectoral tip and both tail lobes are uniform olive-grey — the black/white fin-tip markings, the one defining must-read, are completely absent, leaving the generic Shark construction with an olive hue shift.

Tall dorsal, five gill slits and a longer-upper-lobe tail are present, but the crescent mouth set under the snout — a named must-read — is entirely invisible: the area below the eye to the snout tip is blank, unlike the toothed jaws its neighbours carry.

Dark vertical stripes clearly band the flank and teeth mark the jaw, so tiger reads; but the snout keeps the same pointed taper as the others instead of a blunt square front, and the upper tail lobe is the standard fork, not a long trailing lobe.

No terminal mouth spans the front of the head (same tapered profile as neighbours), no flank ridges, and the flank shows only dark smudges over the dot lattice every tile shares — no white-spot checkerboard; it reads as a slightly bulkier generic grey shark, not a whale shark.
Three plain orange ovals in the crown with no grey kidney nut hanging beneath any of them; reads as an apricot tree, and the defining must-read nut is invisible.
Ringed trunk, arching feather fronds and a husked brown nut wedged at the frond base read coconut instantly; only one nut instead of a cluster and no trunk lean.
The spiky yellow fruits sit perched on top of the canopy like flowers instead of hanging heavy from branches — the hanging must-read is wrong and the fruit reads small.
A leafless vertical stack of round green balls with short brown upright spikes on top — reads as a brussels-sprout stalk; catkins are neither yellow nor dangling and there is no multi-stemmed bush.
Radiating lance leaves and orange fruit dangling below the crown edge on a stalk make the mango read; fruit lacks the kidney shape and the wiry stalks are short.
Plainly the Coconut construction reused — pinnate feather fronds and a nut-like cluster on a ringed brown trunk; no lobed palmate leaves and no melons packed against the trunk.
Wide blob crown instead of the upright narrow oval, fruits read as yellowish rounds, and the white five-petalled blossom must-read is absent — a stranger would say apple.
Green false trunk and paddle blades are right, but the harvest is a cluster of small yellow spheres at the crown centre — no hanging bunch of straight green fingers at all.
Red fruits ringed with green-tipped radiating hairs in tight pairs are unmistakably rambutan; the crown is wispy and mid-green rather than the dense dark dome.

Front/head is the tallest point, not the rump — the exact opposite of the must-read silhouette; muzzle is dark not tan, no tall rounded ears; it is the same grey-hued template as the bottom-row bears.

No dished concave face (brow is heavy and convex with a drooping blob muzzle), no long pale digging claws (feet are dark stubs); the height at the front comes from the oversized head, not a muscular shoulder hump.

Plainly the same construction as the Brown Bear next door with only slightly more orange streaking; no visible shoulder hump distinct from the huge head, no dished profile, claws are dark not long and pale.

A stranger would say panda — white body, dark eye smudges on a white face, black band with dark legs at the front — but the band sits mid-torso rather than cleanly joining black forelegs and the eye patches are smears, not teardrops.

White and longer-bodied, but the head is the same huge round domed skull as every other bear in the strip on a short neck — the small narrow Roman-nosed head on a long neck is wrong, and the paws are small dark stubs, not huge furred ones.
Mid-grey coat with no shoulder mane, no pale U/Y chest blaze anywhere, and the muzzle is the same short dark blob as its neighbours instead of a long pale mobile snout; no curved claws visible.
No pale cream eye rings or facial patches at all — the one diagnostic marking is invisible; otherwise a hue-shifted copy of the Sloth Bear beside it.
No golden-cream chest crescent visible, coat is dull grey rather than sleek jet black, no long curved claws; it is the Black Bear/Sloth Bear template again with only the hue changed.

Slender legs and no tail are there, but the topline is flat — no arched back rising to the rump — and the woolly texture makes it read as a brown lamb, near-identical chassis to the Capybara beside it.
Big blunt heavy squared muzzle, tailless barrel body and high-set dark eye read capybara; gaps are the sheep-like wool texture and the rump sitting level with the shoulders instead of higher.
Body is a legless round ball, not the long low tubular form the must-read demands; apart from the thin curled tail it is the same buck-toothed blob chassis as Prairie Dog and the voles.
The long slim deer-like legs are present, but the tall rabbit-like ears are missing — only a small dark nub ear — so the white woolly body reads as a lamb, not a mara.
A legless sphere with big white buck teeth; the stubby tail and small flat ears are invisible, and it is plainly the vole blob construction with the hue changed to tan.
Blunt muzzle and buried ears are fine, but no stubby tail is visible, no legs at all, and the prominent white buck teeth read naked-mole-rat; identical shape to Water Vole with only the hue changed.
The must-read half-body-length furred tail is entirely absent — the rear is a bare curl — and the panel is the same blob as Vole recolored darker brown.

Wings are short thin blades on a ball body, not immensely long plank wings; bill is a small plain yellow wedge with no hook or tube nostrils; near-identical construction to Snow Petrel with only a hue shift.
Reads as a gull — clean white body, grey wing mantle, yellow bill and yellow legs, wing crossing past the tail — but the bill tip shows no hook and the wingtip is dark grey rather than black.

Bill is a long thin needle with no tube nostrils visible on top; brown ball-body-plus-blade-wing build is the same construction as Skua next to it with only the hue changed — a stranger would say generic wader/bird.

Black cap/back, white underside, big orange bill and orange feet do read puffin, but the bill is a long down-curved toucan-like cone rather than triangular and flattened, and the orange/blue-grey bill stripes and clear white face patch are missing.
No heavy hooked bill (small thin dark bill), no white flash at the primary bases anywhere on the wing, and it is plainly the same construction as Petrel one cell over with a slightly warmer brown.

All-white plumage is there, but the short black hooked bill with tube nostrils is not visible (face shows only a tiny dot), and the whole build duplicates the Albatross cell with the hue nudged — same-construction fail.
Small distinct disc and five thin kinked arms read brittle star, but the arms are only ~2.5x the disc width and mostly straight, not the snaky whip arms the must-read demands.
Rounded blunt head with one eye dot on a rib-ringed cylindrical body — no arrowhead head, no paired cross-eyed spots, no auricles, and the ring texture reads segmented; a stranger says slug or leech.
Tall upright white chitin tube with blood-red feathery plumes erupting from the top and no face anywhere; every must-read is visibly present and it names itself.
The inchworm arch and fine ring segments are there, but the body is a round cylinder tapering to a point and I can find no sucker at either end — two must-reads invisible; it reads as an earthworm.
Coin-flat cream disc with a five-petal etching reads sand dollar face-on, but the petal pattern is faint thin lines and the velvety spine fuzz of a living one is absent.
Identical construction to the Giant Tube Worm one row up — same cream banded tube, same red plume, not even a hue change — so it has no read of its own in this strip.

Saw the huge rounded ear, dark blotches on the tan torso and a clear white tail tip; but the patchwork is two-tone (dark-on-tan, no white/black patches) and the legs are stocky rather than lean and long.

All-white fluffy coat and a dense bushy tail read instantly and it is clearly distinct from its neighbours; but the ears are nearly lost white-on-white and the muzzle reads slightly pointed rather than blunt and short.
The bushy tail is carried up-and-out behind, not hanging low as the must-read and note require; and it is plainly the same construction as the Jackal next to it with only the tan hue shifted.
Same body, pose, ears and raised tail as the Coyote with only a warmer tan — a hue-swap clone; the tail is carried high, not low, and I could not see a dark tail tip.

Grey coat, bulkier frame and a dark-tipped bushy tail separate it from the tan pair and a stranger would say wolf; but the tail angles upward instead of level-or-low and the head is not notably broad or blocky.
Upswept needle bill reads instantly and is unique in the strip; but the pied patterning is soft grey instead of crisp black, and the legs are yellow, not the blue-grey the must-read demands.

The smoothly downcurved bill — the make-or-break identifier — is clearly visible and distinct from every straight-billed neighbour; bill is shorter than the quarter-profile ideal and the wading legs are stubby.

Cinnamon breast has zero dark chevron barring and the bill has no pale base; legs are yellow, not dark. With the barring absent it is plainly the same construction as the Snipe with only the hue changed.
All-black bird with no white blocking anywhere, thin yellow legs instead of stout pink, and no visible red eye ring — three of four must-reads missing or wrong; only the orange bill survives.
Long straight bill is there, but the eye sits mid-head (not high and far back) and there are no bold cream back stripes — it is the Curlew chassis with a straightened bill and the same tan hue.

Bill is a tiny straight yellow cone with no sharp downward bend, legs are short and yellow instead of extremely long pink with a backward ankle, and the neck shows only a slight curl, not a long S; apart from pink hue it is the same round-body/short-leg construction as the Heron and Stork beside it.

Pointed dagger bill is present, but the neck is a gentle single curve rather than folded back in an S, and the legs are the same short yellow stubs as every neighbour — no stilt legs or long trailing toes; it differs from the Stork only in grey hue.

The long thin smoothly downcurved bill is clearly rendered and the scarlet body makes the species nameable; remaining gaps are secondary — legs are shorter than the must-read calls for and bare face skin cannot be distinguished from the uniformly red head.

The bill visibly flares into a rounded spatula at the tip on a pink body, so a stranger could name it; bare face skin is not shown and the legs are short rather than long — cosmetic/secondary gaps on the shared chassis.

Bill is medium-length and slightly drooping, not long/heavy/straight; the neck curves exactly like the Heron's instead of being held straight; legs are short and yellow, not very long and red — it reads as a white re-hue of the Heron construction.

Leaves are flat feather-veined broadleaf shapes, not rigid swords; no black terminal spine or edge teeth visible at 4x zoom, and it shares the identical rosette+stalk construction with the neighbouring Aloe.

Tall bare stalk with packed orange-red flower clump reads, and some leaf edges show tooth serration; but blades render flat and feather-veined rather than thick fleshy curving upward, and tubular downward-hanging flower shape is not resolvable.
Drawn as a generic ribbed green cactus dome with one pink apex flower; the swollen grey bulbous caudex, stubby branches, and tip-only leaves are all absent — every must-read missing.

Overlapping paddle pads finally landed, but the magenta tunas ringing the pad edges are completely absent, areoles are only faint scratch lines with no spine tufts, and the lone yellow bloom floats detached above the plant.
Sword rosette and cream bell spike read well, but the curly white threads along the leaf edges — a listed must-read — are invisible even at 4x zoom; edges are clean highlight lines only.
Center marking is a loose spiral scribble, not concentric growth rings, and no pale foot or siphons protrude anywhere from the smooth cream oval.
Same ovoid-plus-seam construction as the Clam with a cyan hue swap; no fluted wavy zigzag lips (seam is straight) and no bulging fleshy mantle between the valves.
Dark tapering silhouette is mussel-ish, but the shell shows no growth lines and the byssal beard threads (a must-read) are completely absent.
Smooth, symmetric closed ovoid identical to the Clam's build in gray; no ruffled layered texture, no unequal cupped/flat valves, no pearly interior visible.
Same chassis as Spider Monkey minus the tail; arms are ordinary medium curves, not the dominant proportion, and hands are round blobs with no hook shape.
Long grey tail is there, but the face is pale grey instead of black, there is no crown crest, and the build is the shared chunky pot-belly, not slender and long-limbed.
Ringed black-and-white tail and white ruff landed, but the face has no fox-like muzzle, no black mask, and the eyes are small and dark instead of bright orange-gold staring.
Limbs are the same thick stubby arms as all three neighbours, nothing spindly; it reads as the Gibbon art with a brown hue and a tail added.
Flat spiral coil, not a fast S-curve; body rope-thick not whip-thin; identical construction to the other three with only a grey hue.
Must-read 'draped in loose loops across branches' absent — no branches, just the same flat spiral; no pointed snout, body thick not pencil-width.
No needle-thin aspect-12 body, no dart-shaped snout, no keyhole pupils; it is the neighbouring coil with a yellow-green hue.
Coil is uniform thickness — the long tapering tail-half must-read is missing; same spiral-and-tongue asset in olive.
No pink backswept crane's-head flowers anywhere — only red berry clusters; and the mat is a single floating upturned crescent, not a wiry creeping mat over bog moss.

Leaves are long needles spreading at wide angles off the stems — the must-read demands scale leaves hugging the stem, not spreading — and the form is a tall stem-fan bouquet (same chassis as Oleander beside it), not a low wiry twiggy mound; it reads as lavender.

Each stem tip bears one large pink scalloped flower with a big speckled brown central disc — a daisy/zinnia, not dense terminal heads of pink pinwheel flowers; wands and narrow leaves are right but the flower construction is the wrong species.

Foliage mass is a blurry medium-green cloud instead of silver-grey felted foliage, no three-toothed wedge tip is visible on any leaf, and the trunk is a tiny plain brown V rather than a twisted gnarled trunk with shredding grey bark.

Barbels present, but body wears a full diamond scale-mesh (must be scaleless), head tapers instead of broad/flat, and no stiff dorsal or pectoral spine is visible — generic forked-tail fish with whiskers.

Back texture can pass for scales and the head is smooth/conical, but the tail is a thin rope-like curl instead of the thick tapering body-length tail; with the long thin snout it reads as an anteater or opossum.

Yellow plumage and a real woven hanging nest with entrance hole land, but the bird stands upright on the ground beside the nest rather than clinging upside down to it, and no black face mask is visible — the body also reads as wicker basketry, not feathers.
Orange with black-edged white bars reads clownfish, but only two bands are clearly visible and the dorsal fin is spiky, not rounded paddle.
Spines radiate evenly all around like a pufferfish/urchin — no dorsal fan, no feathery wing-like pectoral rays, and the banding has no white; a stranger would not say lionfish.
Turquoise body with a visible pale beak plate reads parrotfish, but the forehead bulge is subtle and no large paddle pectoral fin is discernible.
Flared lip and knobby spire are present, but no stalked eyes anywhere — the only dark dots are spire knobs, nothing peers from under the lip despite eyes:prominent.
Glossy egg-smooth shell and a dashed toothed slit read fine, but no patterned mantle flaps fold over the shell — only a pale speckled patch that reads as a highlight.
Good ribbed cone with radiating ridges, but the apex reads centered and the shell floats over a drop shadow — no rock, nothing clamped flush, despite the sessile must-read.
Square-tipped tail must-read is invisible — the body ends in a bare rounded rear — the bill is a tiny nub rather than stout and pointed, and the construction is identical to the Raven cell beside it.
Reads as a magpie: bold white belly crescent against black and a tail longer than the body; but the tail clubs outward at the tip instead of tapering as a graduated wedge.
Same round-bodied build as the Crow with no differentiation — no massive curved bill, no shaggy throat hackles, and no visible wedge tail; all three must-reads are missing.
No legs or talons at all despite biped perched spec; beak is a tiny flat yellow wedge with no hook, cere, or brow ridge — reads as a round-bodied songbird, not an eagle.

Same round-body construction as the Eagle with the hue shifted grey: no white underside, no dark eye-mask stripe, no M-shaped wings, no talons, and it is perched-shaped rather than flying (spec aspect 2.2).

Bare pink head is present, but the feather ruff renders as a white egg-shaped blob on the flank, the posture is the same un-hunched round chassis as its neighbours, and the beak is a small yellow wedge, not a heavy hooked tearing beak.
Rotund sheep-like blob, not a cat silhouette; spots scattered not in rows, no neck stripes visible, and the short thick tail is invisible against the rear.

Banded black-tipped tail is present, but legs are slim and medium-length instead of short and stocky, and the head shows one tall upright ear rather than a broad flattened head with low wide-set ears.

Ringed black-tipped tail and full tabby striping both read, distinct from its neighbours; but the base coat is too white so stripes read zebra-like, and the build is not visibly heavier than a house cat.

The brown spike is a loose speckled cluster, not a dense velvety cigar, and the leaves are a wide drooping fountain with tips falling to the ground — the vertical-strap-leaves must-read is plainly wrong; silhouette is wider than tall against a 0.35 aspect. Reads as fountain grass in seed.

Single dead-vertical symmetric tuft with a radiating root clump: no blades leaning one way with the current, no horizontal creeping rhizome with shoots at intervals, no meadow of parallel straps in sand — all three must-reads missing. Reads as a generic leafy tuft.

Open branching seed head sits at the very top as a fan of thin dark spokes over a tall grass, with a visible grain column beneath it — the species reads. Gaps are secondary: grains are fat tan beads stacked on the stalk instead of narrow purple-brown grains on the branches, the fan is stiff rather than airy, and no water glints at the base.

Pointed stacked-triangle pyramid, not a flat-topped crown with horizontal branch plates; tan cones hang mid-canopy instead of standing upright like barrels on branch tops — all three must-reads missing.

Rendered as a conifer tree, but the reference is the poison-hemlock HERB: no purple-blotched hollow stem, no fern-cut leaves, no white umbrella flower heads — wrong organism, and it is the identical construction to Cedar with a hue shift.

Same squat pyramid-and-straight-trunk build as its neighbours; no tall narrow column, no buttressed flaring base, no cinnamon-red fibrous ridged bark — the trunk is plain smooth brown and only the canopy green differs.
Yellow spoke-ray umbel is present, but the foliage is coarse pinnate fronds with discrete oval leaflets — reads as a fern, not the must-read cloud of thread-fine feathery threads.
Scape is dead straight with a white dome head (no curling loop) and no papery bulb with clove divisions is visible — the base is bare shadow; also near-identical to the Onion beside it.
Leaves read as flat blades, not hollow round tubes, and there is no swollen papery bulb or wiry root fringe; same construction as Garlic with only trivial differences.
White-feet must-read inverted: both visible paws are dark chocolate brown and the lower legs are darker than the sandy body; the only white is on the tail tip. Coat and erect triangular ear do read.

Black-stockings must-read invisible: legs are body-orange their full length with only tiny dark paw nubs that disappear at strip scale. The big white-tipped brush tail, pointed ears and narrow muzzle otherwise read as fox.

Round hamster-like blob, not aspect 3.2: tail is a short curled stub (must-read says half total length), limbs are vertical stubs not splayed sideways, no loose neck skin; tongue forked but red not yellow. A stranger would guess a spotted rodent.

Long snake-like neck and deeply forked flicking tongue ARE there and it reads as a lizard, but the tail is a thick round curl about body length (must-read: laterally flattened, LONGER than body) and the limbs end in clawless round stubs — 'large hooked claws' invisible.
Short pointed fish snout, not the long tweezer beak; a tall triangular dorsal fin where the must-read demands a low ridge instead; no melon — reads as a pink fish.

Blunt curved-mouth head, paddle flipper, streamlined body and notched flukes read as whale with a blowhole nub on the crown; but the nub floats slightly off the head outline and the fluke is drawn face-on like the neighbouring fish tail, so horizontal orientation is only implied.

Crown is a rounded puffball, not a flat-topped umbrella in horizontal layers; flowers are golden wattle pom-poms which the note explicitly forbids (should be cream puffballs); no paired white thorns at nodes, only scratch marks on the trunk. Feathery pinnate sprigs are present but two of three must-reads are missing.

The defining swollen grey barrel trunk is absent — trunk is a thin brown stick like the Acacia's; crown is a dense leafy ball instead of stubby root-like branches; gourds sit embedded in the canopy rather than dangling on long stalks. Reads as a generic fruit tree, not a baobab.

Colour is right, but the art is three broad flame-shaped blades with pale midribs — the must-read fine repeatedly forking branch structure is absent, and the base is a spidery tan root cluster, not a small disc holdfast.
